body.stem: Your team opens the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics workspace la-backup. The tiles and grids that cover the workloads protected in the Recovery Services vault come back empty, while the same workbook returns rows for the workloads in the Backup vault over the same period. Both vaults have been sending logs to this workspace for several weeks, so ingestion lag does not explain the gap. You want the reports to populate for the Recovery Services vault. Which change should you make?

rows: Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations
Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations

options.text: Republish prod-rsv's rsv-diag setting so the six Azure Backup events are sent in Resource specific mode instead of Azure diagnostics mode.
Add the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event to prod-rsv's rsv-diag setting so it keeps being sent in Azure diagnostics mode.
Republish prod-bv's bv-diag setting so the six Azure Backup events are sent in Azure diagnostics mode instead of Resource specific mode.
Remove Addon Azure Backup Storage Data from prod-bv's bv-diag setting and add the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event to it in Resource specific mode.

explanation.correct: For a Recovery Services vault, the six Azure Backup events reach the Backup reports only when they are sent in Resource specific mode; when they are sent in Azure diagnostics mode, no data appears in the reports. prod-rsv currently sends those events in Azure diagnostics mode, which is exactly why its tiles and grids are empty, whereas prod-bv (a Backup vault) already uses Resource specific mode and therefore returns rows. Republishing rsv-diag with the same six events under Resource specific mode creates the dedicated per-event tables in la-backup (for example CoreAzureBackup and the Addon tables) that the workbooks query, and that is the recommended target mode for new settings.

perChoice.b: The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is supported only in Azure diagnostics mode, so adding it to that setting would indeed flow data, but the Log Analytics reporting solution is moving off the legacy event: it is on a deprecation path and the reports will cease to support data from it. The workbooks read the new per-event tables, so this change does not fill the empty tiles and keeps the estate on the route that is being retired.
perChoice.c: prod-bv is already returning data, and for Backup vaults all diagnostics events are sent to the resource-specific tables only, so there is nothing to migrate there. Republishing that setting to Azure diagnostics mode would put a working feed at risk and would not affect prod-rsv, which is the vault with the empty tiles.
perChoice.d: A diagnostic setting carries a single log mode, and the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event flows no data at all when it is sent in Resource specific mode, so the second half of this change cannot work. Addon Azure Backup Storage Data is also not applicable to a Backup vault, because storage consumed and frontend size already arrive through Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data, so removing it changes nothing. This also targets the vault whose reports are already populating.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects a group of Azure VMs, and your team reviews backup activity through the Backup Job History report in a Log Analytics workspace. On the morning of 29 March, with the time range set to the last 7 days, a colleague compares the report's job grid with the vault's own job list and points out two oddities: a job that started late on 23 March is filed under a date earlier than the day it actually completed, and the jobs that ran after midnight on 29 March do not appear in the report at all. You need to explain the report's counting behaviour to the colleague. Which statement is correct?

exhibit.text:
Backup Job History grid, Time Range = Last 7 days, viewed on 29 March
(row 3 comes from the vault's own Backup jobs blade, not from the grid)

Date shown in report | Backup item | Start time (UTC) | End time (UTC) | Outcome
23 Mar              | Daily-VM-01 | 23 Mar 23:50    | 24 Mar 00:06    | Succeeded
24 Mar              | Daily-VM-02 | 24 Mar 22:10    | 24 Mar 22:52    | Succeeded
Not listed          | Daily-VM-03 | 29 Mar 02:00    | 29 Mar 02:47    | Succeeded

options.text: A job is counted in the range in which it was triggered rather than the one in which it finished, and the report ends at the close of the last completed UTC day, so jobs triggered during 29 March are not listed yet.

A job is counted in the range in which it finished rather than the one in which it was triggered, and the report ends at the close of the last completed UTC day, so jobs triggered during 29 March are not listed yet.

A job is counted in the range in which it was triggered rather than the one in which it finished, and the report includes everything up to the moment the workbook is opened, so jobs triggered during 29 March are listed as they run.

A job is counted in the range in which it finished rather than the one in which it was triggered, and the report includes everything up to the moment the workbook is opened, so jobs triggered during 29 March are listed as they run.

explanation.correct: The report shows job details for the jobs that were triggered inside the selected time range, not for the range in which they completed, and the reports never include the current partial day: they always cover full UTC days, so on 29 March the data ends at 23:59 UTC on 28 March and jobs created on 29 March only appear when the report is viewed on 30 March. That is why the job that started at 23:50 on 23 March and ended after midnight on 24 March is filed under 23 March, and why the job that started at 02:00 on 29 March is absent.

perChoice.b: Wrong on the attribution half: job details are shown for jobs triggered in the selected range, not for the range in which they completed, so a job that started at 23:50 on 23 March and finished after midnight still belongs to 23 March. The statement about the last completed UTC day is right, but the counting rule it applies to is not.
perChoice.c: Wrong on the day-coverage half: the report never shows the current partial day; it always uses complete UTC days, which is why jobs from 29 March are missing while the report is viewed on 29 March. The trigger-time part of the statement is correct.
perChoice.d: Wrong on both halves: jobs are attributed to the range in which they were triggered, not the one in which they finished, and the report excludes the current partial day instead of including everything up to the moment the workbook is opened.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault in West Europe that sends diagnostic logs to the Log Analytics workspace la-backup-prod in East US 2. The workspace retention is set to 30 days, and the compliance team wants a 12-month trend of backup job outcomes read from the Backup Reports workbook in Log Analytics. You need that reporting period to cover the full 12 months. Which action should you take?

rows: Resource specific mode, six Azure Backup events
Backup Reports workbook in Log Analytics

options.text: Increase the retention of la-backup-prod to 365 days; the workspace can stay in East US 2 while the vault remains in West Europe, even in a different subscription.

Keep the retention of the la-backup-prod workspace at 30 days in East US 2 and add a diagnostic destination that sends the vault's logs from West Europe to a storage account in the same region and subscription as the vault, then assemble the 12-month trend by querying the archived log files.

Keep the retention of la-backup-prod at 30 days in East US 2 and enable the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event in Azure diagnostics mode so that the Backup Reports workbook shows the 12-month trend.

Increase the retention of la-backup-prod to 180 days and reconfigure the vault's diagnostic setting to Resource specific mode with the six new events so that the Backup Reports workbook covers the full 12 months.

explanation.correct: Azure Backup reports are rendered by workbooks whose Kusto queries run against the Log Analytics workspace, and data in that workspace is retained for 30 days by default, so the retention period has to be extended whenever a longer reporting horizon is required. Raising the retention on la-backup-prod to 365 days makes a full year of history queryable by the Backup Reports workbook. The location and subscription of the workspace are independent of the vault that feeds it, so a workspace in East US 2 and a vault in West Europe in different subscriptions need no relocation.

perChoice.b: Archiving the vault's diagnostic logs in a storage account is the option for keeping raw logs for custom analysis; it does not feed the Backup Reports workbook, whose widgets query the Log Analytics workspace. With the workspace still at 30 days, the workbook cannot cover 12 months. A Recovery Services vault can also only send diagnostic logs to a storage account located in its own region.
perChoice.c: The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is supported only in Azure diagnostics mode and is on a deprecation path, and the Log Analytics reporting solution is also ceasing support for data from it; it is kept only for existing custom queries and visualizations. Enabling it does not change the workspace's 30-day retention, so the workbook still cannot show a 12-month trend.
perChoice.d: Using Resource specific mode with the six new events is the recommended way to feed the reports, but a 180-day retention is far shorter than the requested 12-month horizon, so the workbook would still return only about six months of data.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects a group of Azure VMs, and its backup logs already reach a Log Analytics workspace where the workbook tiles show job outcomes. You need the on-call rotation to be notified whenever Azure Backup raises an alert about a protected item, using a notification path that remains supported going forward. Which change should you make?

rows: Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations

options.text: Create an Azure Monitor alert and route the fired alert through an alert processing rule and an action group that targets a logic app, webhook, or runbook.
Enable the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category in the vault's existing diagnostic setting and let the classic alerts solution notify the on-call rotation.
Enable the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category in the vault's existing diagnostic setting and pair it with an Azure Monitor action group that targets a logic app.
Create an Azure Monitor alert that queries the Addon Azure Backup Alerts table in the workspace every five minutes, without an alert processing rule or action group.

explanation.correct: The classic alerts solution has been deprecated in favour of Azure Monitor-based alerting, so the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category should not be selected for this. The supported pattern is to create an Azure Monitor alert, then use an alert processing rule to route the fired alert and an action group that invokes a logic app, webhook, or runbook to reach the on-call rotation.

perChoice.b: This depends on the classic alerts solution, which is deprecated; the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category should not be selected. Notification should come from an Azure Monitor alert combined with an alert processing rule and an action group.
perChoice.c: Selecting the deprecated Addon Azure Backup Alerts category is the part to avoid, even though an action group is attached to it. An action group alone does not replace the deprecated event; the alert should be created in Azure Monitor and passed through an alert processing rule to an action group.
perChoice.d: The query depends on data from the Addon Azure Backup Alerts category, which is deprecated and is not among the categories enabled in the vault's diagnostic setting, so the query would return no usable data. On top of that, omitting both an alert processing rule and an action group leaves no target that can notify the on-call rotation.

body.stem: You have a Backup vault named bv-prod that ships its diagnostic data to the Log Analytics workspace la-backup, and your analysts read the Backup Reports workbook there. The vault's current diagnostic setting is shown below. You need the workbook to keep reporting storage consumption while the vault does not send the same information to the workspace twice. Which change should you make?

rows: Core Azure Backup Data; Addon Azure Backup Job Data; Addon Azure Backup Policy Data; Addon Azure Backup Storage Data; Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data; Azure Backup Operations

options.text: Remove Addon Azure Backup Storage Data from the diagnostic setting; the storage consumed and frontend size already arrive through Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data.

Remove Core Azure Backup Data from the diagnostic setting; the storage consumed and frontend size already arrive through Addon Azure Backup Storage Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data.

Remove Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data from the diagnostic setting; the storage consumed and frontend size already arrive through Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Storage Data.
Keep all six events in the diagnostic setting; the storage consumed and frontend size arrive through separate tables for each of the six events.

explanation.correct: For a Backup vault, the frontend size and the backup storage consumed are already part of Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data, so the Addon Azure Backup Storage Data event is not applicable to Backup vaults and selecting it only produces a redundant table. Removing that event leaves the workbook's storage figures intact while avoiding a second copy of the same numbers.

perChoice.b: The Addon Azure Backup Storage Data event does not apply to a Backup vault, and Core Azure Backup Data is the main event that carries the baseline vault data; dropping it would remove information the reports rely on rather than a duplicate of it.
perChoice.c: Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data carries the frontend size figures, so removing it would lose values the workbook displays; the event that does not apply to a Backup vault is Addon Azure Backup Storage Data.
perChoice.d: Leaving all six events selected keeps the Addon Azure Backup Storage Data table in place for a Backup vault, where that event is not applicable and yields a redundant table next to the data already delivered by Core Azure Backup Data and Addon Azure Backup Protected Instance Data.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that ships its backup diagnostics to a Log Analytics workspace through a single diagnostic setting, and your operations team still has custom Kusto queries that read the vault data from the shared diagnostics table. You want the Azure Backup workbooks to begin returning job information while those custom queries keep returning rows during the changeover. Which change should you make?

rows: Backup Job History tiles in the workbook

options.text: Change the existing diagnostic setting to enable Resource specific and select the six new Azure Backup events, removing the Azure diagnostics mode.
Add a second diagnostic setting to enable Azure diagnostics and select the six new Azure Backup events, and keep the existing diagnostic setting until the custom queries are migrated.
Add a second diagnostic setting to enable Resource specific and select the six new Azure Backup events, and keep the existing diagnostic setting until the custom queries are migrated.
Remove the existing diagnostic setting and add one that enables Resource specific with the six new Azure Backup events selected.

explanation.correct: For a Recovery Services vault, the Backup reports only pick up the six new Azure Backup events when they are sent in Resource specific mode, so a setting in that mode is required before the workbook can show job information. The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event, by contrast, carries data only in Azure diagnostics mode, so the existing setting has to stay in place while the custom queries that read the shared diagnostics table are rewritten against the new per-event tables. Keeping one setting for the legacy event and a second setting for the six new events lets both operate during the changeover, and the legacy setting can be retired once the queries are migrated.

perChoice.a: Switching the existing setting over to Resource specific withdraws the Azure diagnostics path that the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event depends on, so the custom queries that read the shared diagnostics table stop returning rows as soon as the change is applied instead of after a planned migration.
perChoice.b: The six new Azure Backup events are honoured by the Backup reports only when they are sent in Resource specific mode. A second setting that uses Azure diagnostics mode therefore leaves the workbook without job data.
perChoice.d: Removing the existing setting cuts off the only supported route for the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event, which works solely in Azure diagnostics mode, so the custom queries break before they have been rewritten against the new tables.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects 420 Azure VMs, and your analysts read the Backup Reports workbook in a Log Analytics workspace. The Cloud Storage and Protected Instances tiles return identical figures whichever time range the analysts pick, and they have concluded that the range filter has no effect on the report. You need to correct their understanding of how these two tiles are produced. Which statement is correct?

columns: Time range selected in the workbook

options.text: The values are point-in-time snapshots taken at the end of the selected time range, so narrowing the range does not change them.
The values are point-in-time snapshots taken at the start of the selected time range, so narrowing the range does not change them.
The values are the sum of the daily values across the selected time range, so narrowing the range should reduce them.
The values are the daily average across the selected time range, so narrowing the range should reduce them.

explanation.correct: In the Backup Reports workbook, the Cloud Storage and Protected Instances figures are point-in-time readings captured at the close of the selected time range, not totals accumulated across that range. That is why the exhibit shows the same 2.41 TB and the same 418 items for every range the analysts pick: the tiles reflect the state of the estate at one moment, while job, schedule and policy-adherence widgets re-aggregate the underlying records for each range.

perChoice.b: This option describes a reading taken when the range opens. The report captures the storage and protected-instance values once, at the close of the selected range, so a start-of-range reading is not what the tiles contain, and a start-of-range value would normally shift when the range is moved.
perChoice.c: A sum would grow as the range widens and shrink as it is narrowed, so the exhibit's constant 2.41 TB could not be a sum. These two tiles report the value as it stands at the close of the selected range rather than a total over the period.
perChoice.d: An average would also vary with the range that is selected, which contradicts the constant figures shown for the Protected Instances tile. The tile reads the instance count once, at the close of the selected range, and repeats that reading for every range.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects Azure VMs with Azure Site Recovery and also uses a recovery plan, and your analysts open the Azure Site Recovery Job History report in the Backup Reports workbook. The table below shows the operations that were recorded in the vault on 12 April. You need to identify which of these operations the report is expected to list. Which set of operations should you expect?

columns: Operation recorded in the vault on 12 April
rows: Nightly backup of the application VMs
Backup of the Azure File share

options.text: The failover test of the estate triggered from the recovery plan and the failover of the single VM triggered on the replicated item.
Only the failover test of the estate triggered from the recovery plan; the failover of the single VM triggered on the replicated item is excluded.
Only the failover of the single VM triggered on the replicated item; the failover test of the estate triggered from the recovery plan is excluded.
All four operations, including the nightly backup of the application VMs and the backup of the Azure File share along with the failover test of the estate and the failover of the single VM.

explanation.correct: The Azure Site Recovery Job History report lists only the jobs that were triggered on replicated items and recovery plans. In the exhibit, the failover test of the estate was triggered from the recovery plan and the failover of the single VM was triggered on the replicated item, so both operations belong in this report. The scheduled backups of the application VMs and the Azure File share are backup operations rather than Azure Site Recovery jobs, so they are not listed by this report.

perChoice.b: This drops the failover of the single VM, but that job was triggered on a replicated item, and jobs triggered on replicated items are included in the Azure Site Recovery Job History report alongside the recovery plan operations.
perChoice.c: This drops the failover test triggered from the recovery plan, yet jobs triggered on recovery plans are also included in the Azure Site Recovery Job History report, so the estate failover test belongs in the results.
perChoice.d: This pulls in the scheduled backup jobs for the application VMs and the Azure File share. Those are backup operations recorded by the vault, and this report covers only the Azure Site Recovery jobs triggered on replicated items and recovery plans.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects Azure VMs and SQL databases hosted on those VMs, and your analysts read the Azure Backup workbooks in a Log Analytics workspace. Before each review meeting they pick a Time Range in the workbook and export the trend charts for the pack listed below. You need to state how the workbook plots the points for each pack, what it does with a Time Range that starts and ends partway through the day, and whether SQL log backup activity appears at all. Drag each outcome to the matching place.

columns: Time Range entered in the workbook

items.text: Daily grouping
Weekly grouping
Monthly grouping
Excluded — no rows shown
Widened — 00:00–23:59 UTC

slots.label: Operations review
Service review
Annual compliance pack
Ad-hoc window
SQL log backup activity

explanation.correct: Chart aggregation follows the length of the selected Time Range: a span of 30 days or less yields one point per day, a span greater than 30 days and no more than 90 days yields one point per week, and anything larger yields one point per month. The Operations review range (1–7 October, 7 days) is therefore plotted per day, the Service review range (1 August – 29 September, 60 days) per week, and the Annual compliance pack range (1 November 2025 – 31 October 2026, 365 days) per month. A Time Range that starts and ends partway through the day is widened out to whole UTC days, so the ad-hoc window (14 April 16:45 to 15 April 09:30) is really reported as 14 April 00:00 to 15 April 23:59 UTC. SQL log backup jobs are not displayed in the Backup Reports workbook, so that activity is excluded and returns no rows.

perChoice.i1: Operations review (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-07). The span is 7 days, inside the 30-days-or-less band, so the workbook plots one point per day.
perChoice.i2: Service review (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-29). The span is 60 days, greater than 30 and no more than 90, so the workbook plots one point per week.
perChoice.i3: Annual compliance pack (2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31). The span is 365 days, beyond the 90-day band, so the workbook plots one point per month.
perChoice.i4: SQL log backup activity. SQL log backup jobs are not displayed in the Backup Reports workbook, so the job grid returns nothing for them.
perChoice.i5: Ad-hoc window (2026-04-14 16:45 to 2026-04-15 09:30). The workbook overrides the time part of the selected window and runs the query across whole UTC days, i.e. 14 April 00:00 to 15 April 23:59 UTC.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault that protects several hundred Azure VMs; your operations team reviews backup activity in the Azure Backup workbooks in a Log Analytics workspace. After an analyst rearranged the widgets on one of the tabs, the team disagrees about the behaviour of the tiles, the drop-downs, the entries. You need to pin down the behaviour that applies in each situation below. Drag each outcome to the matching place.

exhibit.text:
Layout of one tab of the Backup Reports workbook
-------------------------------------------------
Widget                       Position in the tab
Subscription drop-down       Top line, first column
Resource group drop-down     Top line, second column
Protection stopped tile      Top line, third column
Protected entries list       Second line, first column
Backup success trend         Second line, second column

items.text: Reaches only the widgets placed on the right or underneath it; the widgets on its left or above stay untouched
Cannot be selected, so it cannot filter the widgets below it
Narrows the grids plus charts underneath it, keeping only the rows carrying the value it displays
Only items still present when the period ends are included

slots.label: The drop-down you moved to the top of the tab: the widgets it covers
A tile with no color
The coloured tile showing a count for a single state of protection: the entries shown underneath it
A protected resource deleted partway through the window you chose

explanation.correct: In the Azure Backup reports, filters are applied from left to right and top to bottom, so a filter only reaches the widgets positioned to its right or beneath it and never those to its left or above. Tiles that carry no color are not selectable at all, while choosing a colored tile narrows the grids and charts underneath it to the records that carry the value shown on the tile. Separately, the reports list only the backup items and backup policies that still exist at the end of the selected time range, so anything deleted midway through the range is absent from the report.

perChoice.i1: Belongs with the drop-down moved to the top of the tab: filters run from left to right and top to bottom, so this drop-down reaches only the widgets to its right or beneath it and leaves the widgets to its left or above unchanged.
perChoice.i2: Belongs with the tile that has no color: tiles that are not colored are not selectable, so such a tile never filters the widgets beneath it.
perChoice.i3: Belongs with the colored tile: selecting a colored tile filters the grids and charts below it so that they show only the records that pertain to the value on the tile (for example, the Protection stopped tile narrows the grids and charts below to the backup items in that state).
perChoice.i4: Belongs with the deleted resource: the reports display only the backup items that exist at the end of the selected time range, so an item deleted in the middle of the range is not displayed, and the same convention applies to backup policies.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault named rsv-prod, and the workloads it protects are listed below. Five colleagues each want a different view of the vault's backup activity, and you have to point each of them at the right entry in the Azure Backup workbooks. Drag each entry to the request it satisfies.

exhibit.text:
Vault rsv-prod - protected workloads

Azure virtual machines ............. 12   Daily at 01:00 UTC
Azure Files file shares ............ 3   Daily at 02:00 UTC
PostgreSQL server ................. 1   Weekly on Sundays
Azure Blobs (operational tier) .... 2   Daily at 03:00 UTC
Azure Disks ....................... 4   Daily at 04:00 UTC

items.text: Backup Reports
Backup Configuration Status
Backup Job History
Backup Schedule and Retention
User Triggered Operations

slots.label: One consolidated view of storage usage, protected instances, policy adherence and optimization across every workload type in the vault
Which of the virtual machines in the vault have a backup policy assigned
How each backup of the PostgreSQL server, the Azure Blobs and the Azure Disks ended during the period
The run times and the number of days that the Azure Files shares are kept
The backup runs that people in the on-call team kicked off manually inside this Recovery Services vault

explanation.correct: The consolidated request is answered by Backup Reports, which is the single view that brings together jobs, instances, usage, policies, policy adherence and optimization for every supported workload type, matching the colleague who wants an estate-wide overview. The question about which virtual machines are covered is answered by Backup Configuration Status, the entry that states which VMs are configured for backup and which the documentation limits to Azure VM. The request about how each backup of the PostgreSQL server, Azure Blobs and Azure Disks ended is answered by Backup Job History, whose coverage list includes PostgreSQL server, Azure Blobs and Azure Disks. The request about run times and how long the Azure Files shares are kept is answered by Backup Schedule and Retention, which covers Azure VM and Azure Files. The runs the on-call team started by hand are listed by User Triggered Operations, which is scoped to the Recovery Services vault in the scenario.

perChoice.it1: Fits the request for one consolidated view spanning every workload type: Backup Reports is the single view covering jobs, instances, usage, policies, policy adherence and optimization, so it answers the estate-wide overview request.
perChoice.it2: Fits the request about which virtual machines are covered: Backup Configuration Status is the entry that states which VMs are configured for backup, and it applies to Azure VM only, which matches the request.
perChoice.it3: Fits the request about the outcome of each backup run: Backup Job History covers VM, MARS, MABS, DPM, PostgreSQL server, Azure Blobs and Azure Disks, so it covers the PostgreSQL server, Azure Blobs and Azure Disks named in that request.
perChoice.it4: Fits the request about run times and how long data is kept: Backup Schedule and Retention covers Azure VM and Azure Files, and the request concerns the Azure Files shares in the vault.
perChoice.it5: Fits the request about runs that people started by hand: User Triggered Operations lists those runs and is scoped to the Recovery Services vault described in the scenario.

body.stem: You are setting up how the backup data from the Recovery Services vault rsv-prod reaches the team's reporting pipeline, and you can create extra resources wherever the current landscape doesn't fit. Four requirements are waiting to be met. Drag each option to the requirement it satisfies.

items.text: The storage account in East US 2
A storage account in West Europe
The event hub in West Europe
The Log Analytics workspace in East US 2, using Resource specific mode with the six Azure Backup events
Assign the built-in Azure Policy definition that adds a Backup diagnostic setting to the subscription, with Owner access on each subscription

slots.label: Archive the vault's raw data so the team can run its own analysis on it later
Stream the vault's backup data to a processing platform that runs outside Azure
Give the analysts the Azure Backup workbooks with their tiles and grids
Give every vault under your management that currently ships nothing, or only the legacy pooled data, a supported way to send its data, without editing them one by one

explanation.correct: Each requirement is met by the destination or configuration that matches its purpose: a Recovery Services vault may write diagnostic logs only to a storage account in its own region, so the archive copy has to go to a West Europe account (st-logs in East US 2 cannot be used); streaming the events to another system is done through an event hub; the Azure Backup reports and workbooks are rendered from a Log Analytics workspace, which may live in a different region from the vault, and for a Recovery Services vault the six new events are honoured in the reports only when they are sent in Resource specific mode; and the built-in Azure Policy definition can add a diagnostic setting to every vault in a scope that has none or only a legacy setting, so assigning it at subscription scope with Owner access on each subscription brings the remaining vaults into reporting without editing them one by one.

perChoice.i1: The storage account in East US 2 fits no slot: a Recovery Services vault can send diagnostic logs only to a storage account in the same region, and rsv-prod is in West Europe, so this account cannot be used to archive the vault's data.
perChoice.i2: It belongs with the archiving requirement: a storage account is the destination for raw logs kept for custom analysis, and because the vault can only write to a storage account in its own region, an account in West Europe is needed.
perChoice.i3: It belongs with the streaming requirement: an event hub is the destination used when backup events must be streamed to another system.
perChoice.i4: It belongs with the workbooks requirement: the reports and workbooks are read from a Log Analytics workspace, which for this vault can sit in a different region (East US 2), and the six Azure Backup events are honoured in the reports of a Recovery Services vault only in Resource specific mode.
perChoice.i5: It belongs with the estate-wide requirement: the built-in Azure Policy definition can add a diagnostic setting for every vault in a scope that has none or only a legacy setting, and it can be assigned to a whole subscription, provided you have Owner access on each subscription.

body.stem: You have the Azure Backup workbooks that a reporting team reads in the Log Analytics workspace la-backup, which is fed by the Recovery Services vault rsv-prod. The team's standing questions about what the workbook contains and how quickly it settles are listed below. You need to pair each answer with the question it answers. Drag each answer to the matching question.

items.text: Up to 24 hours
About 48 hours after the change
Only entries that still exist when the range ends
Weekly and monthly groupings, where a month spans four weeks

slots.label: Once the vault's diagnostics are switched on, how soon can the first records be expected in the workspace?
How long should reviewers be told to wait before treating freshly configured figures as complete?
Which protected items and their schedules does the workbook include when some were removed partway through the chosen period?
Which breakdown levels are offered for an item whose protection schedule runs once every seven days?

explanation.correct: The first push of diagnostic data into a Log Analytics workspace can take up to 24 hours, so "Up to 24 hours" answers the question about when the first records can be expected. Microsoft advises starting to view the reports about two days after a diagnostics change, so "About 48 hours after the change" answers the waiting-time question. The workbook lists only the backup items and policies that still exist at the end of the selected range, and anything removed partway through disappears from the report, so "Only entries that still exist when the range ends" answers the question about which items and schedules appear. In the Policy Adherence grids an item on a weekly schedule has no daily view, offering weekly and monthly breakdowns only, and a "month" there counts as four weeks (28 days) with partial weeks excluded, so "Weekly and monthly groupings, where a month spans four weeks" answers the breakdown-levels question.

perChoice.i1: Matches the question about how soon records appear in the workspace: after diagnostics are configured, the initial data push can take up to 24 hours.
perChoice.i2: Matches the question about how long to wait before relying on newly configured figures: Microsoft recommends starting to view the reports about two days (roughly 48 hours) after the change.
perChoice.i3: Matches the question about which protected items and schedules appear: only backup items and policies that still exist at the end of the selected range are listed, so items deleted partway through vanish from the report.
perChoice.i4: Matches the question about breakdown levels for a schedule that runs every seven days: in the Policy Adherence grids such an item offers weekly and monthly views (no daily view), and a "month" there counts as four weeks (28 days), so partial weeks are excluded.

body.stem: You are reviewing how backup data from a set of Recovery Services vaults reaches the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics. The notes below list the five points that are still open from that review, and the list of steps that follows holds the moves your team has drafted to close them. You need to attach one step to each open point, and any step that settles none of them should be left out. Drag each step to the matching point.

exhibit.text:
Point 1: rsv-we runs in West Europe. Every event record it produces must be kept for seven years in a storage account, and the workbook data keeps coming from the workspace la-backup in East US 2.

Point 2: Twelve vaults in the subscription have no diagnostics setting. They must all reach the workspace, and the operations team does not want to open each vault one by one.

Point 3: Compliance has asked for the names of the vaults that are still sending the older event instead of the current one.

Point 4: Governance compares items on a weekly schedule with items on a daily schedule in the policy adherence grids and wants to know how the period buckets behave.

Point 5: The BI team still runs the old template app that read backup data from a storage account; the platform group has said that route will stop being supported.

items.text: Create the storage account in the same region as the Recovery Services vault.
Replace the Power BI template app and the V1 schema with the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics, because that route is on a deprecation path.
Assign the built-in Azure Policy definition that adds diagnostics settings to the vaults in scope, with Owner access on each subscription.
Run the documented Kusto query that unions AzureDiagnostics with CoreAzureBackup and returns the vaults found only under AzureBackupReport.
Treat a month in the policy adherence grids as four weeks, and expect the items on a weekly policy to have no daily view.
Point the stored copy at a storage account in a different region, since the vault's location does not limit where the copy is written.
Enable the Azure Backup Reporting Data event on the remaining vaults so that their rows appear in the reports.
Add the Addon Azure Backup Alerts event to the diagnostics setting so that the workspace receives the backup alerts.

slots.label: Point 1 — archival of the seven-year event records
Point 2 — covering the estate without manual effort
Point 3 — the search that names the stragglers still on the old event
Point 4 — the bucketing rule behind the two schedule types
Point 5 — the retirement of the team's old tooling

explanation.correct: Each open point is settled by exactly one of the drafted steps. The archival requirement for rsv-we is met by creating the storage account in the vault's own region, because a Recovery Services vault can only send diagnostic logs to a storage account in the same region, while the Log Analytics workspace may sit in another region or subscription. Bulk coverage of the twelve vaults with no diagnostics setting is met by the built-in Azure Policy definition that adds a diagnostics setting to the vaults in scope, which can be assigned to a subscription or a resource group and requires Owner access on each subscription. The compliance request for names is met by the documented Kusto query that unions AzureDiagnostics with CoreAzureBackup and returns the vaults found only under AzureBackupReport. The policy adherence question is met by treating a month as four weeks (28 days, so partial weeks drop out) and by knowing that items on a weekly policy have no daily view. The retirement of the team's tooling is met by moving onto the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics, since the Power BI template app that sourced data from a storage account and the V1 schema are on a deprecation path. The remaining three steps settle no point: a storage account in another region is not allowed for a Recovery Services vault, the legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is honoured only in Azure diagnostics mode and therefore does not populate the backup reports for a Recovery Services vault, and the classic backup alerts event should not be selected at all.

perChoice.i1: Belongs at Point 1. The seven-year archive of rsv-we's event records goes to a storage account, and a Recovery Services vault may only send diagnostic logs to a storage account located in the same region as the vault, so the storage account is created in West Europe. The workspace in East US 2 is unaffected, because a Log Analytics workspace may be in the same or a different region.
perChoice.i2: Belongs at Point 5. The earlier Power BI template app that sourced backup data from a storage account is on a deprecation path, and the V1 schema is on a deprecation path in favour of the supported V2 schema, so the reporting has to run on the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics.
perChoice.i3: Belongs at Point 2. The built-in Azure Policy definition adds a diagnostics setting to every vault in the assigned scope that has none or only a legacy one, it can be assigned to a whole subscription or a resource group, and you must have Owner access on each subscription to assign it.
perChoice.i4: Belongs at Point 3. The documented Kusto query unions AzureDiagnostics (Category 'AzureBackupReport', OperationName 'Vault', SchemaVersion_s 'V2') with CoreAzureBackup and returns the vaults found only under AzureBackupReport, which is how the vaults still sending the older event are listed by name.
perChoice.i5: Belongs at Point 4. In the policy adherence grids a month is counted as a four-week (28 day) period so that partial weeks are excluded, and items on a weekly backup policy have no daily view at all — only weekly and monthly views exist for them.
perChoice.i6: Settles no point. A Recovery Services vault can send diagnostic logs only to a storage account located in the same region, so the stored copy cannot be redirected to a storage account in a different region.
perChoice.i7: Settles no point. The legacy Azure Backup Reporting Data event is supported only in Azure diagnostics mode, and for a Recovery Services vault the current events are honoured only in Resource specific mode, so enabling the legacy event does not populate the backup reports; that event is also on a deprecation path.
perChoice.i8: Settles no point. The Addon Azure Backup Alerts event belongs to the classic alerts solution, which is deprecated in favour of Azure Monitor-based alerts, so it should not be selected in a diagnostics setting; fired Azure Monitor alerts are routed with an alert processing rule and an action group.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault rsv-prod that protects 195 Azure VMs, and your compliance analysts read the Azure Backup workbooks in the Log Analytics workspace la-backup. The backup policies applied to the VM groups inside the vault are listed below. Two of the analysts have asked how the Policy Adherence grid behaves for one of those groups, and you need to answer both of them correctly.

exhibit.text:
VM group   | Backup policy frequency | VMs protected | Policy retention
vm-group-a | Daily                   | 120           | 14 days
vm-group-b | Weekly                  | 45            | 8 weeks
vm-group-c | Monthly                 | 30            | 1 year

body.statement: For the rows that belong to vm-group-b, the Policy Adherence grid offers {{views}}, and a single monthly bucket covering those rows spans {{month}}.

options.text: a weekly and a monthly view
a daily, weekly and monthly view
a daily view only
an hourly and a daily view
28 days
30 days
31 days
the exact length of each calendar month

explanation.correct: The Policy Adherence grids follow an aggregation logic similar to the report charts, with two differences for items whose backup policy runs on a weekly schedule: there is no daily breakdown for those items, so only the weekly and monthly views are available, and a 'month' in those grids is counted as a four-week period (28 days) rather than 30 days, which keeps partial weeks out of the results. vm-group-b is on a weekly policy, so the analysts get the weekly and monthly views, and each monthly bucket spans 28 days.

perChoice.month:month_b: For rows on a weekly policy the monthly bucket is measured as four weeks, that is 28 days, precisely so that partial weeks are left out; it is not a 30-day period.
perChoice.month:month_c: As with the other monthly option, this grid does not follow a 31-day period for these rows; the monthly bucket is a fixed four-week (28-day) window.
perChoice.month:month_d: The grid deliberately uses fixed four-week (28-day) months for rows on a weekly policy instead of tracking calendar months, and that fixed length is what excludes partial weeks from the monthly figures.
perChoice.views:views_b: The daily breakdown is not offered for rows whose policy runs weekly; only the weekly and monthly views appear for them, so this option lists a view the analysts will not find in the grid.
perChoice.views:views_c: Rows protected on a weekly schedule have no daily breakdown at all in the Policy Adherence grid; the weekly and monthly views are the ones on offer, so this option is wrong in both directions.
perChoice.views:views_d: There is no hourly breakdown in the Policy Adherence grid, and rows on a weekly policy also lose the daily one, so neither view listed here is available for these rows.

body.stem:
You are responsible for backup visibility across the Recovery Services vaults listed below, which protect the company's Azure VMs, SQL databases and Azure Files shares. Your analysts read the Azure Backup workbooks in Log Analytics, and those workbooks are meant to cover every vault in the estate, but several of the vaults are not feeding them the way the workbooks expect. Editing each vault by hand would take weeks, so you plan to use a built-in Azure Policy definition that adds diagnostics settings to Azure Backup vaults and apply it across the estate instead.

Which statement about that built-in definition is correct?

rows: Azure Backup Reporting Data, sent in Azure diagnostics mode
Azure Backup Reporting Data, sent in Azure diagnostics mode
Six current Azure Backup events, sent in Resource specific mode

body.statement: The built-in definition can be assigned to {{scope}}; it adds a diagnostics setting for {{targets}}; and applying it across your estate requires {{access}}.

options.text: a whole subscription or a resource group
a whole subscription or a single vault
a management group or a resource group
a whole management group or a resource group
vaults with no diagnostics setting or with only the Azure Backup Reporting Data event
vaults with a diagnostics setting or with only the six current Azure Backup events
vaults with no diagnostics setting or with only the six current Azure Backup events
vaults with a diagnostics setting or with only the Azure Backup Reporting Data event
Owner access on each subscription
Contributor access on each subscription
Owner access on each resource group
Reader access on each subscription

explanation.correct: The built-in Azure Policy definition adds a diagnostics setting for every vault in the assigned scope that has none or only the legacy setting, it can be assigned to a whole subscription or a resource group, and assigning it requires Owner access on each subscription. So the correct completions are: the assignment scopes a whole subscription or a resource group; the target set of vaults with no diagnostics setting or with only the Azure Backup Reporting Data event; and Owner access on each subscription. In the table, that means rsv-app-02 (nothing configured) and rsv-app-01 and rsv-sql-01 (only the legacy event) get a new setting, while rsv-web-01, already sending the six current events, is left alone.

perChoice.scope:b: This pairing offers a single vault as an alternative scope. For this definition the documented assignment scopes are a whole subscription or a resource group, and a single-vault scope is not one of them, so the vault-by-vault goal would not be met as described.
perChoice.scope:c: A management group is not among the assignment scopes listed for this definition. The documented choices are a whole subscription or a resource group, so leading with a management group is incorrect.
perChoice.scope:d: This pairing leads with a management group, which is not one of the scopes listed for this definition. The documented choices are a whole subscription or a resource group.
perChoice.targets:b: This would add settings to vaults that already have one, including the ones already sending the six current events, and it would skip the vaults whose only setting still sends the Azure Backup Reporting Data event, which are exactly the vaults that need new settings.
perChoice.targets:c: This covers the vault with nothing configured but skips the two vaults whose only setting still sends the Azure Backup Reporting Data event, so those two would keep leaving the workbooks empty.
perChoice.targets:d: This treats every vault that already has any setting as a target, including rsv-web-01, which already sends the six current events and therefore needs nothing. The definition only adds settings where there is none or only the legacy setting.
perChoice.access:b: Contributor-level permissions are not sufficient to make this assignment. The documented requirement is Owner access on each subscription.
perChoice.access:c: Owner access on the resource group alone does not meet the documented requirement, which is Owner access on each subscription, so the assignment across the whole estate could not be completed.
perChoice.access:d: Reader access is read-only and cannot be used to assign a policy definition. The documented requirement is Owner access on each subscription.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault rsv-prod that protects your production Azure VMs, and you are adding two diagnostic destinations to it: a storage account to archive the raw backup logs for your own analysis, and a Log Analytics workspace that feeds the Azure Backup workbooks your reporting team reads. Neither destination has been created yet, and the security team wants to know how the platform constrains where each of them may sit. Which placement is correct?

rows: storage account sa-backup-archive - region not yet chosen
Log Analytics workspace la-backup - region not yet chosen

options.text: The storage account must match the vault's region; the Log Analytics workspace need not.
The Log Analytics workspace must match the vault's region; the storage account need not.
Both destinations may sit in any region.
Both destinations must match the vault's region.

explanation.correct: A Recovery Services vault can send its diagnostic logs only to a storage account that sits in the same region as the vault itself, so sa-backup-archive would have to be created in North Europe. The Log Analytics workspace is the flexible one: it may live in the vault's region or in another region (and even in another subscription), so la-backup can be placed elsewhere and still receive rsv-prod's data and populate the Azure Backup workbooks.

perChoice.placement:b: This reverses the two constraints. It is the storage account that is tied to the vault's own region; the Log Analytics workspace is the destination that is allowed to sit in another region.
perChoice.placement:c: Neither destination is unconstrained. Because a Recovery Services vault can only archive its diagnostic logs to a storage account in the vault's own region, both cannot be placed in any region.
perChoice.placement:d: This is too strict on the reporting side. A Log Analytics workspace in another region still receives the vault's diagnostic logs, so the two destinations are not both forced into the vault's region.

body.stem: You have a Recovery Services vault whose backup items and policies are reported through the Backup Reports workbook in Log Analytics. The changes in the exhibit were made in that vault during March, and your analysts set the Time Range to 1-31 March. You need to know what the workbook shows for that range. Which statement is correct?

rows: Deleted on 20 March, when the virtual machine was unregistered from the vault

body.statement: For the 1-31 March range, the workbook's grids {{outcome}}.

options.text: list neither the deleted backup policy nor the deleted backup item for the virtual machine
list the deleted backup item for the virtual machine only for 1-19 March and the deleted backup policy only for 1-9 March
list the deleted backup policy for the whole range but omit the deleted backup item for the virtual machine throughout
list both the deleted backup policy and the deleted backup item for the virtual machine for the whole range

explanation.correct: The report displays the backup items and the backup policies that still exist at the end of the selected time range, and the same convention applies to policies as to items. Anything deleted part-way through the range is therefore not displayed at all for that range, rather than appearing up to its deletion date. The policy was deleted on 10 March and the virtual machine's backup item on 20 March, so at the end of the 1-31 March range neither object exists, and both are absent from the grids.

perChoice.outcome:b: This option assumes the workbook keeps a day-by-day history of the range. The grids are built from the backup items and policies that exist at the end of the selected range, so an object deleted during the range drops out entirely instead of being shown up to the day it was deleted.
perChoice.outcome:c: A backup policy follows the same rule as a backup item: once it has been deleted, it is not listed for the range in which the deletion happened, even for the days on which it existed. The policy is therefore absent from the March grids along with the virtual machine's backup item.
perChoice.outcome:d: This option treats a mid-range deletion as if the objects had survived for the whole range. Both objects were deleted before 31 March, so both are left out of the 1-31 March grids.

body.stem: You support a mixed estate, and the inventory below shows the assets and the protection they have today. Two colleagues each need a different view: the inventory lead wants the assets that no solution protects at all, and the service owner wants, for every item already covered by backup, its most recent backup status and the most recent point it can be restored from. Neither of them wants to write a Kusto query. Which entry should each of them open?

rows: Azure Backup and Azure Site Recovery

body.statement: The inventory lead should open {{estateView}}, and the service owner should open {{perItemView}}.

options.text: Resiliency: Protected Items
Resiliency: Protectable resources
the Backup Configuration Status report in the workbook
the Overview pane of the vault
the Backup Jobs blade inside the vault
the Backup Instances list inside the vault
the Backup Configuration Status report in the workbook
the Backup Schedule and Retention report in the workbook

explanation.correct: Resiliency is the portal's cross-solution view: it splits the estate into Protected Items (assets covered by one or more protection solutions) and Protectable resources (assets that no solution currently protects). The inventory lead is after the second group, so the Protectable resources view is the entry that names the unprotected SQL databases and File shares, and it needs no Kusto query. For the per-item view, the Backup Instances section inside the vault lists each backup item of the workload type together with its last backup status and the latest available restore point, which is exactly what the service owner asked for.

perChoice.estateView:a: Resiliency: Protected Items lists the assets that are covered by one or more solutions, so it would show the protected VMs instead of the databases and shares that have no protection at all.
perChoice.estateView:c: The Backup Configuration Status report states which Azure VMs are configured for backup; it is Azure VM only, it lives in the Log Analytics workbook rather than the portal, and it says nothing about the databases or file shares that are unprotected.
perChoice.estateView:d: The Overview pane of the vault summarises alerts, jobs, security and usage for that single vault; it does not enumerate the assets that are not protected by any solution.
perChoice.perItemView:a: The Backup Jobs blade lists the backup jobs that ran in the vault rather than the protected items themselves, so it does not give each item's last backup status or the most recent point it can be restored from.
perChoice.perItemView:c: The Backup Configuration Status report only says which Azure VMs are configured for backup; it does not show each backup item's last backup status or latest available restore point, and it does not cover file shares or databases.
perChoice.perItemView:d: The Backup Schedule and Retention report covers the schedule and retention applied to Azure VM and Azure Files items; it does not provide per-item last backup status and latest available restore point.

body.stem: You support twelve Recovery Services vaults, and the backup data they send lands in the workspace la-backup, where your operations analysts look for job history. You plan to move the remaining vaults off the older single-event stream that carried all of a vault's backup data in one place, and the first step is to produce the list of vaults that still send that stream. The Microsoft-documented audit query works with two sets of rows, one for the older stream and one for the current per-event data, and it returns the vault identifiers that are present only in the older set. You need to fill in those two row sets correctly.

rows: Six per-event tables, one per event

body.statement: To build that list, the audit query reads {{legacyRows}} and compares them with {{currentRows}}.

options.text: the AzureDiagnostics rows where Category is AzureBackupReport, OperationName is Vault and SchemaVersion_s is V2
the CoreAzureBackup rows where Category is AzureBackupReport, OperationName is Vault and SchemaVersion_s is V2
the AzureDiagnostics rows where Category is AzureBackupReport, OperationName is Job and SchemaVersion_s is V2
the AddonAzureBackupJobs rows where Category is AzureBackupReport, OperationName is Vault and SchemaVersion_s is V2
the CoreAzureBackup rows
the AzureDiagnostics rows
the AddonAzureBackupJobs rows
the AddonAzureBackupPolicy rows

explanation.correct: The documented audit for finding vaults that still send the legacy single event unions the rows that the legacy stream wrote into the shared diagnostics table, filtered to Category AzureBackupReport with OperationName Vault and SchemaVersion_s V2, with the rows in the CoreAzureBackup table, and then keeps the vault identifiers found only under the legacy category. The first row set therefore has to come from AzureDiagnostics with exactly those three filters, and the second row set has to come from CoreAzureBackup, which carries the vault-level records of the current per-event data.

perChoice.legacyRows:a2: CoreAzureBackup is the resource-specific table that the current per-event data lands in, so it holds no rows for the older combined stream. The legacy rows live in the shared diagnostics table under Category AzureBackupReport, which is what the documented audit query filters on.
perChoice.legacyRows:a3: The documented audit query filters the legacy rows down to OperationName Vault, because the vault-level records are what identify which vault sent the data. Filtering to Job returns job records instead of vault records, so the vault identifiers can no longer be derived from the result.
perChoice.legacyRows:a4: AddonAzureBackupJobs is one of the per-event tables created by the current six events, so it never contains the older combined stream. The legacy rows are the ones under Category AzureBackupReport in the shared diagnostics table.
perChoice.currentRows:b2: The shared diagnostics table is where the older combined stream lands, so using it for both sides of the comparison cannot separate the vaults that still send it. The second set has to come from the CoreAzureBackup table.
perChoice.currentRows:b3: AddonAzureBackupJobs holds job data from the current per-event tables, not the vault-level records that show where a vault's data came from. The comparison set used in the documented audit is the CoreAzureBackup table.
perChoice.currentRows:b4: AddonAzureBackupPolicy holds policy data from the current per-event tables. The audit compares the legacy rows against the CoreAzureBackup table, which carries the vault-level records for the current events.
